surprises.description: Distributable earnings before realized losses were $0.24 per share, 2 cents below the $0.26 consensus, even though that result was within the preview author's $0.24–$0.25 estimate. The much lower $0.07 per share after realized losses reflects a separate, unexpected credit event.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Distributable earnings before realized losses were $18.1 million ($0.24 per share)”

surprises.description: Converting a multifamily loan to REO triggered a $13 million realized loss and reduced distributable earnings to $0.07 per share, far below the $0.26 consensus. The loss was fully reserved and had no book-value impact, but the preview had identified a sixth REO as a downside risk rather than anticipated this specific conversion and loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Distributable earnings fell to $5.1 million ($0.07 per share) after a $13 million realized loss tied to converting one multifamily loan to REO, which had no book value impact as it was fully reserved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch the ‘4’-rated bucket … for additions, any first ‘5’-rated loan, and whether REO count goes from 5 to 6.”

surprises.description: Total leverage rose to 4.03x, well above the preview's 3.32x starting point and the level above which it said balance-sheet capacity would become a concern. Management said the balance sheet was near target size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total leverage increased to 4.03x from 3.32x at June 30, with management signaling the balance sheet is near target size”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above ~3.4x with a widening discount to book invites a balance-sheet-capacity question.”

surprises.description: Management said future activity would shift to a “one in, one out” pace matching repayments, limiting further portfolio growth. That is more cautious than the preview's focus on an earnings step-up from new originations and its discussion of a pipeline of executed term sheets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management signaling the balance sheet is near target size and future activity will shift toward a ‘one in, one out’ pace matching repayments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 inherits a higher average earning-asset balance” and “~$380M of executed term sheets pending.”

surprises.description: Management reported that CRE CLO spreads had widened about 25 basis points since early September and loan spreads had moved 15–50 basis points wider, a less favorable financing and lending backdrop than the preview's emphasis on FL8's attractive pricing and the debt market's support for the collateral.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRE CLO spreads have widened ~25 basis points since early September, with loan spreads moving 15-50 basis points wider depending on asset quality.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TRTX priced the $1.0B TRTX 2026-FL8 CRE CLO … at an ~87.4% advance rate and SOFR+143” and “the debt market will lend against this collateral at an 87% advance rate and SOFR+143.”

surprises.description: The company approved a new $50 million repurchase authorization after exhausting the prior $25 million plan. The preview highlighted the remaining $9.3 million authorization and identified a fresh or expanded authorization as an important possible signal, but the new authorization was twice the size of the old one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company exhausted its $25 million buyback plan … and the Board approved a new, doubled $50 million repurchase authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only $9.3M remained” and “A fresh/expanded authorization is the cleanest signal management believes its own marks.”
